title: 6 people. Always three.
blocks: Six people at a party. Some know each other, some don't. Here's a promise: there are always three people who all know each other, or three who are all strangers. Always.

Draw each person as a dot. Draw a blue line between two people who know each other, and a red line between two who don't. Every pair gets exactly one line. We're looking for a triangle with all three sides the same color.
With five people, you can avoid it. Put them in a ring, color the ring blue and the star inside red. Look for a triangle of one color. There isn't one.
Add a sixth person, and it breaks. Pick any one person. They have five lines. Five lines, two colors, so at least three of them share a color. Say three are blue.

Look at the three people on the ends of those blue lines. If any line between them is blue, it makes a blue triangle with our person. If all three lines between them are red, they form a red triangle. Either way, there's a triangle.
No matter how you color the lines, you can't escape. Six is the smallest crowd where it's guaranteed. Order hides inside chaos, once the crowd is big enough.
